sourceInformation.source: Keystone Kapers (Activision, 1983), designed by Garry Kitchen. Original characters and department-store setting created for this tribute.
sourceInformation.perspective: Side-on 2.5D orthographic camera, with a full-building security view
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js R180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGPU and WebGL 2 compatibility; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; PeerJS 1.5.5; AI Hub Session Protocol v1, client 1.4.0; Bun bundling
sourceInformation.artDirection: Stylized cel shading and ink outlines; warm lithographic colours; procedural three-dimensional models and embedded typography
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip with custom idle, run, jump, duck, stumble, celebration and propeller tracks
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated ragtime-inspired music, oscillator/noise sound effects, filtered gibberish voices. Music defaults to 10%. No audio files.
sourceInformation.online: 1–4 player shared-world co-op via AI Hub; standalone WebRTC room-code co-op via PeerJS, same-origin BroadcastChannel transport, and two-player couch co-op
sourceInformation.testing: One-command headless suite covering a complete playthrough, mechanics, menus, dev sliders, emulated standard gamepad, phone touch, offline audio, same-origin room synchronization, an actual Internet-signalled WebRTC data channel, and four AI Hub conformance scenarios. Visual composition checked through WebGL compatibility. Physical controller, subjective audio listening and play between physical devices on separate networks: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: 1983 Activision instruction manual archived by AtariAge; AtariAge screenshots; archival descriptions of levels, hazards and sound; Three.js R180 source/docs; Rapier and PeerJS docs; AI Hub Session Protocol v1.

testingFeedback: Seven product issues were found and fixed: HTML embedding, Hub shader startup, quick-travel cooldown, title character placement, duplicate button classes, attract timing, and partial-round Hub statistics. Test-only assertions and expected GPU teardown logs were also corrected. An initial WebRTC test timeout had an unknown cause; the targeted retry passed.
Two were blocking: the initial bundled script did not parse, and shader work delayed some Hub copies beyond automatic readiness. Both are fixed.

The complete three-case playthrough with normal rules, together with all four AI Hub conformance scenarios. The run exercised every hazard, both floor transports, loot, whistles, retries and final victory.
Headless WebGPU screenshots were least helpful because this environment can omit the canvas; renderer state and the WebGL compatibility backend were used for verification and visual inspection.
engineFeedback: Three.js R180 combines procedural modelling, cel shading, native AnimationMixer blending and a WebGPU renderer with a useful WebGL 2 backend.
Yes. Literal dollar sequences in bundled libraries needed replacement callbacks, and first-frame shader work initially blocked Hub readiness. Native asynchronous compilation resolved the latter.
The pursuit simulation and route logic, shared-world co-op, controller menu focus, touch assistance, procedural audio and complete test interface.
Coordinating asynchronous graphics preparation with fixed-step physics and Hub readiness while several copies run in one headless browser.
A first-party controller/menu layer with deterministic game-state testing helpers.
promptFeedback: The research requirement, complete vertical-slice scope, controller-first presentation and explicit attract-mode and dev-tool requirements gave the project a clear target.
The standalone networking transport was unspecified, and the request left the exact format of the source title inside the filename open to interpretation.
Delivering offline single-file play, WebGPU graphics, procedural sound, several input methods and shared-world networking in both standalone and AI Hub environments.
Specify the standalone matchmaking/signalling expectations and whether developer balance controls should remain available in Hub rounds.

aiHub.name: Keystone Kapers: Lift, Laugh, Loot
aiHub.tagline: One crook. Four floors. A whole store full of trouble.
aiHub.description: Chase Bertie Baggs through HalFwick’s department store in three slapstick arcade capers. Leap runaway carts, duck toy planes, take the lift, and bag the bandit alone or with a squad.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick / A D; leap: Cross / Space; duck: Circle / S; lift: Up / W or E, Down to exit; whistle: Square / F; mall view: L1 / Tab; pause: Options / Esc.
